newsitem.title: GERMANY: VE 4-mth W.Europe Passat orders above plan.
newsitem.headline: VE 4-mth W.Europe Passat orders above plan.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Wednesday that incoming orders for its Passat saloon were well above plan in the first four months of 1997, with orders taken for 128,000.

80,000 orders had been expected, VW spokesman Klaus Kocks said, responding to a report in Germany's Manager magazine, which had said the carmaker was threatened with billion-mark losses because of delivery delays.
Kocks said it was a beginner's mistake to speculate that the difference between exploding demand and start-up production was an economic loss, Kocks said.
The report said that there was a bottleneck in production at VW's Emden plant, which would lead to 1.2 billion marks in lost sales.
